## Breaking change
<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important
  to tell them what breaks, how to make it work again and why we did this.
  This piece of text is published with the release notes, so it helps if you
  write it towards our users, not us.
  Note: Remove this section if this PR is NOT a breaking change.
-->

The parameter `context_timeout` is now optional for binary sensors and will default to None. If you've previously not specified this parameter you'll have to adjust your config and add it like this:

```yaml
knx:
  binary_sensor:
    - name: sensor
      state_address: "1/2/3"
      context_timeout: 1.0
```

This prevents users that do not use this feature from waiting one second until automations are triggered.

The parameter `reset_after` for binary sensors expects seconds now instead of milliseconds to streamline the different configuration options. (`context_timeout` also uses seconds)

The parameter `ignore_internal_state` for binary sensors now defaults to False as most users do not use this feature. It defaulted to `True` before.

If you have validation errors of your config after the update and you are using the `operation_modes` parameter for your climate devices please add all erroneous entries to the new `controller_modes` parameter.


## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Updates the underlying library to 0.15.3.

issue_context.title: KNX Binary sensor - Automation 'Already Running'
issue_context.body:
<!-- READ THIS FIRST:
  - If you need additional help with this template, please refer to https://www.home-assistant.io/help/reporting_issues/
  - Make sure you are running the latest version of Home Assistant before reporting an issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/releases
  - Do not report issues for integrations if you are using custom components or integrations.
  - Provide as many details as possible. Paste logs, configuration samples and code into the backticks.
  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem
Since the upgrade to 0.116, logs are filled with warnings on my automations: 'Already running'.
Seems to be caused by the update of xknx to version 0.14.4 (#40472).
My binary KNX sensors now generate 2 events within a few millis.
Simplified example. KNX physical motion sensor sends "turn off actuator", HA binary sensor is listening on related group address. This results in 2 HA state_changed events, where Event2 is produced almost immediately after Event1:
Event1: old_state ("on", counter 0) new_state ("off", counter 1)
Event2: old_state ("off", counter 1) new_state ("off", counter 0)

Since my automations listen on state change "off", they fire twice.

Is this a bug? Then I must not modify my config.
Or is it a feature to have a new state_changed event only because the counter attribute is reset to 0?

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Configuration -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.116
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): < 0.116
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core): HassOS 4.13
- Integration causing this issue: KNX
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/knx

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

```yaml
knx:
  binary_sensor:
  - name: "motion_detector_light"
    state_address: '0/6/6'
    sync_state: False
automation:
  - alias: 'Do Something'
    trigger:
      - platform: event
        event_type: state_changed
        event_data:
          entity_id: binary_sensor.motion_detector_light
    condition:
      condition: and
      conditions:
        - condition: template
          value_template: "{{ trigger.event.data.new_state.state == 'off' }}"
    action:
        - entity_id: light.myLight
          service: light.turn_off
```

## Traceback/Error logs
<!--
  If you come across any trace or error logs, please provide them.
-->

```txt
Logger: homeassistant.components.automation.doSomething
Source: helpers/script.py:1097
Integration: Automation (documentation, issues)
First occurred: October 7, 2020, 5:50:06 PM (843 occurrences)
Last logged: 6:06:36 PM

Do Something: Already running
```

## Additional information

Hey there @julius2342, @farmio, @marvin-w, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`knx`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L231) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

Please add your `binary_sensor` configuration.

From your logs it looks like setting `ignore_internal_state` to `False` will fix this.
Thanks for the proposal, will try it, don't find ignore_internal_state in HA KNX binary sensor documentation however.
Hm that's weird. I'm pretty sure we added that. Will open a PR to fix it.

Thanks Marvin, works indeed again. And to be honest I should have read the tip in the release notes about the new default value. Actually I did read it, but a few weeks ago and I clearly forgot about it :-)

For the readers interested: if ignore_internal_state is True, the binary sensor's state is set in all cases when _set_internal_state is called (and a state change event is produced), even if the state is the same as before. If False, state is only set when it is different than before.

https://github.com/XKNX/xknx/blob/master/xknx/devices/binary_sensor.py

Or just change the automation to verify that the from state isn't off.

It's reasonable common to generate state_changed events even thou the value didn't change. Used for assumed state entities in other integrations.

Hi, very similar to this binary_sensor thing, would it be possible to have the "ignore_internal_state" property for knx "sensors" as well ? For example I am using a sensor with type "scene_number" together with an automation in order to execute some actions within HA when a knx scene number is called, but if the same scene is called two times without any other scene number in between, the value of the HA state is not changed and the automation is not called again. Thank you very much !
Can you not just use a scene for this? https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/knx/#scene

The way I understand it, the "state" of a KNX scene entity in HA does not change when triggered (it stays on "scening") and is only used the other way around (make HA to trigger a KNX scene).
I also used the event listening tool to verify that: triggering a scene on KNX bus did not change the state of the scene entity in HA while listening the "state_changed" event type.
That's why I ended up using the sensor entity instead. But then I have the secondary problem above. The only work-around that I have found so far is to add an extra action at the end of my automation in order to trigger a dummy scene number on the KNX bus. The state of the sensor entity would then be "reset" to this dummy number and ready to be triggered when the target scene number is activated again.

Can you please open a feature request here: https://github.com/XKNX/xknx/issues

Please also state your specific use case. I think it will be possible to add something like this.
I will do it now, thank you very much for the fast feedback
